S27.01.needs: a CLI sign-in to an AGI account that has artifacts; an artifact with no title is optional
S27.01.note: The CLI has no separate card or viewer for artifacts; the title appears on each list line and in the JSON from show. The code audit's line 660 is the list renderer, not a card.
steps: Sign in to the AGI CLI so the account has at least one artifact, and optionally publish or create one.
In a terminal, run: agi artifacts list
Check that each artifact line shows its title after its id and type in brackets.
Find an artifact with no title (if one exists) and check that its line shows "Untitled artifact" instead.
Run: agi artifacts show <id> --json and check that the "title" field matches the list, with "Untitled artifact" when there is no title.
Type /artifacts in the chat and compare the same titles with the list output.
S27.01.where: Type "agi artifacts list" in a terminal, or type "/artifacts" in the chat. Each artifact prints as an id, then its title, then its type in brackets; the title shows "Untitled artifact" when it has none. Run "agi artifacts show <id> --json" to see the "title" field.

labels.text: Print an artifact's content, or write it to a file.

S27.37.needs: a CLI sign-in to an AGI account with a markdown artifact
S27.37.note: The artifact export is the code at lib.rs:1375, and it writes .md only when the artifact type is markdown (or the language is markdown). The chat /export markdown path is for whole conversations, not documents, and was not checked against Expected beyond its existence.
steps: Sign in to the AGI CLI and find an artifact of type markdown with: agi artifacts list
Run: agi artifacts show <id> --out notes (replace notes with a folder or file name you want)
Look at the printed path; it should end in .md for a markdown artifact.
Open the written .md file in a text editor and compare its text with the artifact content shown by agi artifacts show <id>.
Optional: in the chat, type /export markdown my-chat.md and open the file the message names, to check the conversation export.
S27.37.where: Type "agi artifacts show <id> --out <folder or file>" in a terminal. A file path with no extension gains the artifact's extension, and a Markdown artifact gets ".md". For a conversation, type "/export markdown <path>" in the chat.

S27.41.needs: a credential for an email MCP server (a connected email account) and a test address you control
S27.41.note: The prompt only appears when the session can ask for approval, and the body is shown only as the raw argument JSON, with no separate Body line; the approval key labels were not found as visible strings in the code, so the tester should use the prompt's own choices.
steps: Connect an email MCP server in the CLI so a send-email tool is available, and sign in with its credential.
In the chat, ask: "Send an email to <a test address you control> with subject 'QA test' and body 'hello'."
When the approval prompt opens, read its title "Allow MCP tool ... from server ...?".
Check that the detail shows "Who receives it" with the recipient, "Subject" with the subject, and the body in the argument text below.
Decline or allow the call with the prompt's keys and check that the email is sent only after you allow it.
S27.41.where: In the chat, ask the agent to send an email using a connected email tool (an MCP server). The approval prompt "Allow MCP tool '<tool>' from server '<server>'?" appears before the send, and it lists "Who receives it" and "Subject" when those fields are in the call, followed by the full arguments (the body).
